prompt: Match each role to how it talks.
Diego has the knowledge to choose between two designs and needs to think it through. Which role fits?
hint: He lacks nothing but the decision.

choices.text: Sponsoring: put his name forward for the decision
choices.why: Sponsoring opens doors; it does not help him decide.

choices.text: Coaching
choices.why: Right: ask until he finds his own answer.

choices.text: None: leave him alone so he learns by himself
choices.why: A stretch without a net is a test.

choices.text: Mentoring: tell him which one you would pick and why
choices.why: He has the knowledge; telling him takes the decision away.

prompt: Why does the lesson say defaulting to mentoring fails?

choices.text: Junior engineers do not trust advice from senior colleagues
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson suggests that.

choices.text: Mentoring takes too much of the senior person's time
choices.why: Coaching takes more time in the meeting; time is not the argument.

choices.text: He learns the answers, not how to find them
choices.why: Right: the questions he brings stay the same size for a year.

choices.text: Telling is against company policy for staff engineers
choices.why: No such policy.

prompt: What did Hewlett's research on sponsorship find?

choices.text: People with a sponsor asked for and got more stretch work and raises
choices.why: Right: compared with equally qualified people without one.

choices.text: Sponsored people became more skilled than others
choices.why: A sponsor makes work visible, not better.

choices.text: Mentoring and sponsoring had the same effect
choices.why: The lesson separates them because they do not.

choices.text: Sponsorship mattered only in small companies
choices.why: The research was on large companies.

prompt: Put the steps of GROW in order.
items: What will you do, and when?

prompt: Diego's first goal was "senior". What did Lívia do with it?
hint: A title is not a goal.

choices.text: Told him the promotion criteria for senior at Marola
choices.why: That is mentoring, and it skips his own answer.

choices.text: Wrote it down as the goal of the plan
choices.why: A title gives nothing checkable to work towards.

choices.text: Told him a year is too soon to aim for senior
choices.why: A verdict, before any listening.

choices.text: Asked what he would be doing then that he does not do now
choices.why: Right: the second answer was a goal.

prompt: Why does the agenda of the mentoring sessions belong to Diego?

choices.text: Lívia is too busy to prepare one
choices.why: It is a design choice, not a convenience.

choices.text: GROW requires the junior to set the agenda each time
choices.why: GROW is the order of one conversation, not a rule about agendas.

choices.text: Otherwise the mentor becomes a second line manager
choices.why: Right: and Diego already has one, Bruna.

choices.text: Because the sessions are confidential
choices.why: Confidentiality is a separate agreement.

prompt: By Lívia's rough check, past what fraction of the hour spent talking has she been mentoring when she meant to coach? Give it as a percentage, rounded.
Which row of a development plan does the lesson call the most important?
hint: What two people can agree has been met.

choices.text: The check-in schedule with the mentor
choices.why: Needed, but not what makes it checkable.

choices.text: The goal
choices.why: Essential, and still not checkable without the evidence row.

choices.text: The list of courses to take
choices.why: Diego's plan has no course in it.

choices.text: The evidence
choices.why: Right: it turns a plan into something two people can agree was reached.

prompt: Which is a goal in the lesson's sense?

choices.text: Read three books on architecture this year
choices.why: An activity, not a goal.

choices.text: Become a better engineer
choices.why: Not checkable.

choices.text: Lead my feature's review without Bruna stepping in
choices.why: Right: two people can agree whether it happened.

choices.text: Improve communication
choices.why: Not checkable.

prompt: How does the lesson treat the 70-20-10 rule?

choices.text: As a measured finding, good enough to plan training budgets by
choices.why: The percentages were never a measurement.

choices.text: As a myth to ignore
choices.why: The shape is kept: most growth comes from assignments.

choices.text: A rule of thumb from interviews, whose shape holds
choices.why: Right: which is why the plan is mostly assignments.

choices.text: As a requirement: 10% of the plan must be courses
choices.why: Diego's plan has no course.

prompt: By the 1 July check-in, how many times had Diego asked for help after two hours stuck?
Which of Diego's tasks sat in his zone of proximal development?

choices.text: All three, since growth needs every kind of challenge
choices.why: Two of them fall outside the zone, one on each side.

choices.text: Redesigning the database quotas for every team
choices.why: Too many unknowns for one question to unlock.

choices.text: Writing the code for a feature someone else broke down
choices.why: He could already do that alone.

choices.text: Leading the delivery-slot change
choices.why: Right: beyond him alone, within reach with a question or two.

prompt: Order these from least handed over to most.
items: Look into it and tell me; I'll decide
Decide, and tell me before you act
Decide and act; tell me afterwards
Decide and act; no need to tell me

prompt: What made up the net under Diego's stretch? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: Lívia being available, with the two-hour rule
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: A rollout to 5% of customers first
choices.why: Yes: a mistake there is a lesson, not an incident.

choices.text: Lívia rewriting the code before it shipped
choices.why: That would take the stretch away.

choices.text: A review of the design before the team saw it
choices.why: Yes.

prompt: At the September review, what changed in Lívia's role?

choices.text: She became his manager, replacing Bruna
choices.why: Nothing like that happened.

choices.text: She doubled the frequency of their sessions to every week
choices.why: The relationship got lighter, not heavier.

choices.text: She ended all contact, since the goal was met
choices.why: She stayed on as sponsor.

choices.text: Bruna became his mentor and Lívia his sponsor
choices.why: Right: Lívia puts his name forward for design reviews.

prompt: What does the lesson say a senior engineer who mentors nobody is losing?

choices.text: The respect of their peers
choices.why: Not mentioned.

choices.text: Points towards their own promotion at the next review
choices.why: Not the argument made.

choices.text: Their technical skills, which mentoring keeps sharp
choices.why: Mentoring is not described as keeping skills sharp.

choices.text: A view of their organisation they get no other way
choices.why: Right: how new engineers see the system, and where onboarding assumes too much.

prompt: A new engineer on logistics asks Lívia, "Should I learn Kubernetes or Go first?" Following this lesson, what is her best first reply?

choices.text: "Go. Kubernetes can wait."
choices.why: Advice before knowing what she wants.

choices.text: "What would you like to do in a year that you can't now?"
choices.why: Right: the goal first, in her words.

choices.text: "Here is a list of courses for both."
choices.why: Activities without a goal, and mostly training.

choices.text: "Ask your tech lead; I don't mentor people outside checkout."
choices.why: A no with no alternative, and no reason in the lesson.
